title: HIV-1 Transcription Inhibition Using Small RNA-Binding Molecules.
authors: Khatkar, Pooja; Mensah, Gifty; Ning, Shangbo; Cowen, Maria; Kim, Yuriy; Williams, Anastasia; Abulwerdi, Fardokht A; Zhao, Yunjie; Zeng, Chen; Le Grice, Stuart F J; Kashanchi, Fatah
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子抑制剂靶向HIV-1 Tat-TAR RNA互作以抑制病毒转录，虽涉及RNA-蛋白互作和分子对接/模拟，但对象为RNA-蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA，且非TF-DNA体系，方法可迁移但匹配度中等。
abstract: The HIV-1 transactivator protein Tat interacts with the transactivation response element (TAR) at the three-nucleotide UCU bulge to facilitate the recruitment of transcription elongation factor-b (P-TEFb) and induce the transcription of the integrated proviral genome. Therefore, the Tat-TAR interaction, unique to the virus, is a promising target for developing antiviral therapeutics. Currently, there are no FDA-approved drugs against HIV-1 transcription, suggesting the need to develop novel inhibitors that specifically target HIV-1 transcription. We have identified potential candidates that effectively inhibit viral transcription in myeloid and T cells without apparent toxicity. Among these candidates, two molecules showed inhibition of viral protein expression. A molecular docking and simulation approach was used to determine the binding dynamics of these small molecules on TAR RNA in the presence of the P-TEFb complex, which was further validated by a biotinylated RNA pulldown assay. Furthermore, we examined the effect of these molecules on transcription factors, including the SWI/SNF complex (BAF or PBAF), which plays an important role in chromatin remodeling near the transcription start site and hence regulates virus transcription. The top candidates showed significant viral transcription inhibition in primary cells infected with HIV-1 (98.6). Collectively, our study identified potential transcription inhibitors that can potentially complement existing cART drugs to address the current therapeutic gap in current regimens. Additionally, shifting of the TAR RNA loop towards Cyclin T1 upon molecule binding during molecular simulation studies suggested that targeting the TAR loop and Tat-binding UCU bulge together should be an essential feature of TAR-binding molecules/inhibitors to achieve complete viral transcription inhibition.
abstract_zh: HIV-1反式激活蛋白Tat与反式激活应答元件（TAR）在三核苷酸UCU凸起处相互作用，以促进转录延伸因子-b（P-TEFb）的募集，并诱导整合的前病毒基因组转录。因此，Tat-TAR相互作用是病毒特有的，是开发抗病毒治疗药物的有前景靶点。目前，尚无FDA批准的药物针对HIV-1转录，这表明需要开发特异性靶向HIV-1转录的新型抑制剂。我们已鉴定出潜在候选分子，这些分子在髓系细胞和T细胞中有效抑制病毒转录，且无明显毒性。在这些候选分子中，有两个分子显示出对病毒蛋白表达的抑制作用。采用分子对接和模拟方法来确定这些小分子在P-TEFb复合物存在下与TAR RNA的结合动态，并通过生物素化RNA下拉实验进一步验证。此外，我们检查了这些分子对转录因子的影响，包括SWI/SNF复合物（BAF或PBAF），该复合物在转录起始位点附近的染色质重塑中发挥重要作用，从而调节病毒转录。顶级候选分子在感染HIV-1的原代细胞中显示出显著的病毒转录抑制（98.6）。总体而言，我们的研究鉴定了潜在的转录抑制剂，这些抑制剂可能补充现有的cART药物，以解决当前治疗方案中的治疗空白。此外，在分子模拟研究中，TAR RNA环在分子结合时向Cyclin T1移动，这表明同时靶向TAR环和Tat结合UCU凸起应是TAR结合分子/抑制剂实现完全病毒转录抑制的基本特征。
